status_legend.rejected: Candidate family abandoned; not pursued further.
status_legend.diagnostic_positive_sparse: Positive after estimated costs on paper, but too few trades and/or unstable concentration; not robust.
status_legend.frozen: Configuration locked; no further tuning; retained as final diagnostic reference.

B.name: BTC_DOWN_MICRO_H20_CANDIDATE_B
B.objective: Identify tradeable BTC downward moves using microstructure features with strict confidence, edge, and spread filters (DOWN class only, H20).
B.main_change: Post-hoc trade filters on the microstructure feature set (confidence ≥ 0.65, min edge 2 bps, max spread 8 bps, cost multiplier 1.25) applied to direction labels.
B.evaluation_method: Walk-forward paper evaluation with candidate validation and rolling data-slice robustness (recent_halves, recent_thirds, expanding).

robustness.robustness_summary: 7 slices tested; 0 slices with enough trades (min 20); unstable_sparse on full-sample validation (28 sparse buckets).

B.reason: Early strict-config positivity (~5 trades, +3.8 bps) did not survive data expansion and relaxed-filter runs were strongly negative. Threshold/regime tuning rejected 2026-07-09; latest validation remains not_market_ready with unstable_sparse despite marginal full-sample positivity.

C.name: candidate_c_core
C.objective: Improve post-cost paper performance by engineering richer microstructure features instead of post-hoc hour/threshold filters.
C.main_change: candidate_c_core feature set (spread/cost regime, imbalance dynamics, short-horizon returns, time features) with direction labels on walk-forward grids.
C.evaluation_method: 16-config walk-forward candidate grids on BTC/ETH DOWN (20260709T124717) and ETH UP/DOWN (20260709T125740); supplementary per-coin walk-forward runs with binary_tradeable label modes.

metrics.notes: Best grid rank by paper_score; still negative after costs. BTC DOWN H20 best grid: 103 trades, avg −6.99 bps. ETH UP H20: 96 trades, avg −5.15 bps.

robustness.result: negative after costs across all grid configs; no positive post-cost configuration

C.reason: Feature engineering alone did not overcome the cost problem under direction labels. All tested grid configs remained negative after costs; research moved to cost-aware labeling (Candidate D).
C.missing_evidence: Dedicated rolling-slice robustness report for candidate_c_core not located; grid and walk-forward negatives used as strongest evidence.

D.name: cost_aware_labels
D.objective: Reframe labels from direction-only to cost-aware abstention (UP_EDGE / DOWN_EDGE / NO_TRADE and binary tradeable modes) so models skip bars without sufficient edge after fees, slippage, and spread.
D.main_change: Label modes cost_aware_3class, binary_tradeable_up, and binary_tradeable_down with per-row estimated_cost_bps = fee_bps + slippage_bps + spread_bps; diagnostics-only 3-class mode does not support walk-forward training.
D.feature_set: not applicable (label methodology; initial diagnostics used basic features)
D.evaluation_method: Read-only label diagnostics embedded in walk-forward reports; cost_aware_3class runs marked diagnostics_only with zero accepted trades.

robustness.result: diagnostic only for 3-class mode; not predictive enough alone as a standalone candidate

D.final_decision: rejected as standalone candidate; continued as infrastructure
D.reason: Cost-aware labels clarified why direction models lose after costs (~67% NO_TRADE fraction) but did not produce tradeable positive configs on their own. Binary tradeable modes were adopted by Candidates E and F rather than continuing D as an independent model family.
D.missing_evidence: No positive post-cost walk-forward run attributed solely to Candidate D label modes without later feature sets (E/F).

E.name: candidate_e_depth_aware
E.objective: Restore a sparse positive ETH UP H20 signal by adding depth-aware features (bid/ask size, microprice, size imbalance) on top of candidate_c_core.
E.main_change: candidate_e_depth_aware feature set extending candidate_c_core with top-of-book size and microprice features; binary_tradeable_up labels (Candidate D heritage).
E.evaluation_method: Walk-forward paper evaluation and 80-config candidate grid (20260714T071013) with min_trades_after_regime_filter=5.

robustness.result: failed minimum-trade robustness check; grid best configs had only 3 trades

E.reason: Depth-aware features produced a sparse positive ETH UP H20 signal (14 trades, +31.3 bps cumulative) but failed the minimum-trade robustness bar and were too concentrated to promote. Research status recommends rerunning only after more out-of-sample data.
E.missing_evidence: Dedicated Candidate E robustness analyzer report (analogous to candidate_f_robustness) not located.

F.name: ETH_UP_H20_C0.65_E2_M1.25_S8
F.objective: Identify tradeable upward ETH movements using volatility-, spread-, and depth-regime feature interactions.
F.main_change: candidate_f_regime_depth feature set (34 features: candidate_e_depth_aware plus realized volatility, spread/volatility regimes, and interaction terms) with binary_tradeable_up labels and frozen filter thresholds.
F.evaluation_method: Frozen-config walk-forward paper evaluation; Candidate F robustness analyzer; milestone comparison across dataset milestones.

robustness.result: positive after estimated costs but sparse, non-robust, no demonstrated improvement over baseline

F.reason: Candidate F was positive after estimated costs, but trade evidence was sparse, non-robust, and did not demonstrate improvement over the baseline. Configuration frozen for final report reference; no further tuning.

comparison_table.outcome: Rejected — unstable/sparse; early signal did not scale
Rejected — all grid configs negative after costs
Rejected standalone — diagnostic labels only; adopted by E/F
Not continued — positive but below min-trade robustness

missing_evidence_summary: Candidate C: no dedicated rolling-slice robustness report; grid negatives used.
Candidate D: no positive standalone trading run; label infrastructure evidence only.
Candidate E: no candidate_e_robustness report analogous to Candidate F.
